Levels come from the community list of Universal Android Debloater.

Recommended: safe to remove for most people.
Advanced: may break some features.
Expert: can break important functions.
Unsafe: can stop the device from working or starting.

The list is a guide, not a guarantee. Every change made by Able can be undone from the Able archive.
Hides the app and stops it from running. Data is kept.
Removes the app for this user and keeps its data. Able keeps a copy of apps you installed, so they can be restored.
Reinstalls the app for this user from the copy on the device or from Able\'s backup. Its data is kept.
Allow Able in Shizuku to change apps.
Requires Shizuku. You can also use Android App info.
Able does not disable or uninstall itself.

Android archived this app. Restore it from its icon or from the store that installed it.
Android no longer reports this package. Able will try to reinstall it from the copy kept on the device.

The app is hidden and cannot run, show notifications or sync. Its data is kept. Apps or features that depend on it may stop working.\n\nTo undo, open the Able archive and tap Restore, or enable it from Android App info.
The app is removed for the current user and its data is kept. For system apps the copy on the device stays, so it can be restored from the Able archive.
This is an app you installed: Android deletes its APK when it is removed. Able first saves a copy of the APK in its private storage so it can be restored with its data.
You marked this app as protected (for example alarms, messaging or health).
I understand this can break the device or important features
The command was sent, but Android does not report the expected state. Check the app before relying on it.

Closes every process of the app immediately, like Android's Force stop button.

Risk: notifications, alarms and sync stop until the app is opened again; unsaved work may be lost.

Undo: open the app again. Nothing is uninstalled.

Turns the app off for the current user: it disappears from the launcher, cannot run. Its data stays on the device.

Risk: features or apps that depend on it may stop working.

Undo: Able archive, Restore; or Android App info, Enable.

Removes the app for the current user only (pm uninstall -k --user). Its data is kept.

System apps: the APK stays on the system partition, so Restore reinstalls it without a download.

Apps you installed: Android deletes the APK when the app is removed for its only user. Able therefore copies the APK into its private storage first (the size is shown before you confirm). If the copy cannot be made, the app can only be reinstalled from the store; its data is still kept.

Risk: removing system components can break features or, for Unsafe packages, prevent the device from starting.

Undo: Able archive, Restore. A factory reset also restores system apps.

Able remembers every app it disabled or uninstalled, even if Android no longer shows its name.

System apps: Restore reinstalls the copy kept on the device.

Apps you installed: Restore reinstalls the APK backup Able saved before uninstalling. The backup is deleted only after Android confirms the restore, or when you delete it to free space.

Without a backup (for example apps uninstalled before Able kept copies), Android has already deleted the APK: use Reinstall from store. The data was kept, so the app comes back with it.

In every case Able enables the app again if it was enabled before.

Osserva only shows information. Limita in background applies a supported Android restriction while the profile is active. Arresta quando esco force-stops the app after you leave it.

Risk: notifications, sync and alarms can be delayed or missed.

Undo: set the rule back to Osserva at any time. Protected apps are always excluded.

Android lets only system tools disable, uninstall or force-stop other apps. Shizuku is a separate app that gives Able that access after you start it with wireless debugging or root.\n\nWithout Shizuku, open Android App info for the same app: it offers Force stop and, for many apps, Disable or Uninstall.
